title: Darwin-27B-ZTC: A Single-Pass Judge and a Quantitative Look at Its Calibration
gist: VIDRAFT_LAB presents Darwin-27B-ZTC, a 'zero-token classifier' judge that returns a probability distribution over typed answers in a single forward pass, scoring 0.743 zero-shot accuracy on typed-decisions with Brier 0.097 and KL 0.204. The post argues judge quality should be measured by calibration, not just accuracy, and is candid about limits.

insights.claim: LLM-as-judge carries two structural debts: latency from O(L) sequential decoding, which accumulates linearly across millions of items, and unreliable calibration since logprobs diverge from the true posterior while multi-sampling inflates variance and cost.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Cost and confidence quality are the weak points of the dominant evaluation pattern.

insights.claim: Darwin-27B-ZTC treats judging as conditional probability estimation, returning a categorical distribution over each typed question in one forward pass with zero generated tokens.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Replaces decoding loops with classification, making per-judgment cost constant.

insights.claim: Because there is no sampling step, output variance is zero, so reported metrics are exact and reproducible, and temperature, top-p, repetition penalty and max length no longer confound cross-model comparison.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Deterministic judges make benchmark numbers directly comparable and rerun-stable.
insights.quote: Determinism. No sampling step, so output variance is 0.

insights.claim: On the typed-decisions general split, zero-shot and without using the train split, Darwin-27B-ZTC reaches 0.743 overall accuracy over 2,000 judgments with 0 errors.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Headline accuracy figure; applies only to one split of one benchmark.

insights.claim: Accuracy varies by decision type: noul 0.847, choice 0.723, score 0.675, consistent with ordinal scoring being intrinsically harder than categorical judgment.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Per-type reporting shows the weakest area is ordinal scoring.

insights.claim: Calibration is KL 0.204 and Brier 0.097, which the author reads as signal on both correctness and confidence honesty.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Lacks ECE and reliability diagrams, so the calibration claim is only partly evidenced.

insights.claim: The model is claimed to rank number one on the official typed-decisions leaderboard on Hugging Face at 0.743 zero-shot accuracy.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB

insights.claim: When a judge gates a router or safety filter with a confidence threshold tau, overconfidence is fatal because high confidence on a wrong answer leaks through, so accuracy alone cannot evaluate a judge.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Evaluate judges for deployment on calibration, not accuracy alone.
insights.quote: In this structure overconfidence is fatal.

insights.claim: Brier is a strictly proper scoring rule that cannot be gamed by inflating or deflating confidence, and decomposes into reliability, resolution and uncertainty.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: A compact metric that captures both calibration and discrimination.

insights.claim: Accuracy and calibration are independent axes: a model can be accurate but overconfident, or inaccurate but well calibrated.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Both must be reported separately when choosing a model for gating.
insights.quote: The key point is that accuracy and calibration are different axes.
insights.locator: Accuracy and calibration are independent axes

insights.claim: Reliability diagrams and ECE are needed to see which confidence bins are over- or under-confident, which is what is required to choose tau; the author asks the community for guidance on bin partitioning.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: The post's calibration evidence is incomplete until these are published.

insights.claim: Intended fits are large-scale output grading, model routing by confidence threshold, and safety gating, where deterministic calibrated confidence is the design center and better calibration makes tau more stable.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Targets high-volume inference pipelines where per-item decoding cost dominates.

insights.claim: Reported numbers cover only the general split of typed-decisions, calibration is sensitive to distribution shift and needs separate validation, score accuracy is low, and training configuration details are not disclosed while weights, inference method and benchmark scores are public.
insights.speaker: VIDRAFT_LAB
insights.so_what: Real-world calibration under shift is unproven; training details are opaque.
